messages:
lena: quick question — running into odd telemetry behavior with the Go client. Default User-Agent currently includes runtime info + sdk version; security wants a stable UA. Is there an env var or config to pin it? Also tried setting SDK_METRICS_ENABLED=false but I still see outgoing pings to telemetry.redwood.ai. anyone seen this?

jin: hey @lena — there is an override we added for enterprise customers: REDWOOD_SDK_USER_AGENT. it's not fully documented yet. for metrics the canonical flag is REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=off (we've got a mismatch across language libs). what go sdk version?

lena: go client v0.9.1

sam: infra note — tracing headers: we propagate `x-redwood-trace` on the initial request. streaming is a bit special: http streaming uses chunked connection so headers only on handshake. if a stream is retried we create a new connection and will get a new trace id unless the SDK re-injects the header on the retry.

lena: ohh that matches what I saw (different trace ids mid-stream). so for streaming the SDK needs to preserve trace id manually. do we have a recommended pattern/workaround?

jin: exact behavior: for normal HTTP requests the SDK tries to preserve trace id across transparent retries. for streaming we haven't wired the propagation helper into the stream client yet. short-term workaround: set the header explicitly when creating the stream, e.g.:

```go
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, body)
req.Header.Set("x-redwood-trace", traceID)
client.Do(req)
```

or with the SDK helper (not yet on streaming): `tracectx.Propagate(ctx, req)`

lena: thanks. another question: when the SDK does a transparent retry, does it keep the same trace id or create a new one? i saw different ids for what seemed like one logical operation.

sam: retries should preserve the trace id for non-streaming calls. if you see new trace ids it's because the retry path spawned a fresh connection and the SDK didn't attach the header on that retry — that's a bug/edge-case in the client.

jin: i think that's the underlying issue here. i'm opening a small PR to unify env var names and wire trace propagation for streaming. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/312 — adds REDWOOD_SDK_USER_AGENT, recognizes REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS env, and patches streaming client to propagate `x-redwood-trace`. tests included.

lena: perfect — i'll wait for that. any guidance on what a pinned UA should look like from security? they asked we not leak machine details.

sam: prefer a concise pattern: `Redwood-Inference-Go/0.9.1` or `Redwood-Inference/Go-0.9.1`. no runtime/os bits or hostnames. also ensure it can't be user-supplied with PII.

jin: noted. i'll make the env override sanitize input (strip whitespace, max length 128, drop weird control chars) and add a note in the PR.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: go-sdk-ci #312 -> staging at 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC

jin: thanks @deploy-bot. i'll post follow-ups once merged and add a short doc snippet for the enterprise onboarding page (how to pin UA + disable metrics). :thumbsup:

lena: great, thanks both. i'll update our internal onboarding once you ping.

sam: fyi i'll add a short infra note about streaming traces to the ops-runbook so SREs know how to interpret resumed traces.

lena: done — will follow up if anything else pops up.
